Introduction to Game Theory Game theory is the branch of decision theory concerned with interdependent decisions. The problems of interest involve multiple participants, each of whom has individual objectives related to a common system or shared resources. Because game theory arose from the analysis of competitive scenarios, the problems are called games and the participants are called players. But these techniques apply to more than just sport, and are not even limited to competitive situations. In short, game theory deals with any problem in which each player's strategy depends on what the other players do. Situations arise frequently, in all walks of life. A few examples in which game theory could come in handy include: Friends choosing where to go have dinner Parents trying to get children to behave Commuters deciding how to go to work Businesses competing in a market Diplomats negotiating a treaty Gamblers betting in a card game
